messages.text: How Man City plan to argue their innocence in appeal

metadata.summary: Manchester City will argue in their Premier League appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals between 2009 and 2018 came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's owners.
metadata.content: Man City charges: How Premier League club plan to argue their innocence in appeal | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man City charges: How Premier League club plan to argue their innocence in appeal Man City plan to appeal before Friday's deadline after an independent commission found they broke Premier League financial rules by disguising £830m of owner funding as sponsorship income Lyall Thomas Senior Football News Editor @SkySportsLyall Thursday 1 October 2026 17:42, UK Manchester City will argue in their Premier League appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals between 2009 and 2018 came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's owners. An independent commission has found that City broke Premier League financial rules by disguising £830.69m of owner funding as sponsorship income. City's lawyers argued during the 2024 hearing that the funding had come from the Abu Dhabi government, but this was rejected by the commission. metadata.summary: George Russell is hopeful Mercedes' long-awaited car upgrade at the Bahrain Grand Prix will further help his performances as he bids to build on his return to winning ways from Azerbaijan last week.
metadata.content: George Russell: Mercedes driver reveals hope over big Bahrain GP upgrade and says F1 title pressure all on Kimi Antonelli | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content George Russell: Mercedes driver reveals hope over big Bahrain GP upgrade and says F1 title pressure all on Kimi Antonelli Baku victor George Russell declares "I don't feel lost anymore" with Mercedes car and optimistic team's Sepang big upgrade can further help his cause; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Bahrain GP in Malaysia at 5.30am and 9am, live on Sky Sports F1 Thursday 1 October 2026 13:45, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ahead of the Bahrain GP in Malaysia, Kimi Antonelli and George Russell prepare to fight for Drivers' Championship! George Russell is hopeful Mercedes' long-awaited car upgrade at the Bahrain Grand Prix will further help his performances as he bids to build on his return to winning ways from Azerbaijan last week. Russell dominated the Baku event to not only secure his first win in seven races but also claim the maiden 'Grand Slam' of his Formula 1 career, meaning he led every lap from pole position and set the fastest lap. The Briton had been happier with his performances in Mercedes' W17 since the August summer break, yet he had still finished behind title-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli in each of the previous three races, with Antonelli extending his championship advantage to 81 points after victory in Madrid. metadata.summary: Two senior executives at different top-level Premier League clubs have told Sky Sports News they would be "staggered" and "amazed" if 15 clubs were prepared to vote to expel Manchester City from the league, with such a move akin to a "self-inflicted commercial disaster".

Two senior executives at different top-level Premier League clubs have told Sky Sports News they would be "staggered" and "amazed" if 15 clubs were prepared to vote to expel Manchester City from the league, with such a move akin to a "self-inflicted commercial disaster". Expulsion is one of several punishments available to the independent commission, which earlier this week found Man City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them over alleged financial mismanagement. messages.text: Former Wallaby hooker Charles confirms MND diagnosis

metadata.summary: Former Australia rugby international Nathan Charles, who overcame cystic fibrosis to forge a professional career in a contact sport, has been diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND).
metadata.content: Nathan Charles: Former Australia rugby international reveals motor neurone disease diagnosis | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nathan Charles: Former Australia rugby international reveals motor neurone disease diagnosis Nathan Charles has revealed his motor neurone disease (MND) diagnosis; the 37-year-old made four appearances for Australia across 2014 and 2015; Charles overcame cystic fibrosis to produce a decorated career in professional rugby Thursday 1 October 2026 08:23, UK Image: Nathan Charles made four appearances for Australia across 2014 and 2015 Former Australia rugby international Nathan Charles, who overcame cystic fibrosis to forge a professional career in a contact sport, has been diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND). The 37-year-old Charles, who made his Test debut in 2014 and earned four caps for the Wallabies, including a 12-12 draw against New Zealand, revealed he has been diagnosed with the same illness as recently retired National Rugby League star Jai Arrow. MND is an umbrella term for a group of progressive neurological conditions where the motor neurones degenerate. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is the most common form, and ALS is often called Lou Gehrig's disease. During an interview with former Wallabies lock and now commentator Justin Harrison on Stan Sport this week, Charles revealed he had only recently been diagnosed. messages.text: Man City charges: PL players to explore compensation claims if verdict upheld

metadata.summary: Premier League players and their agents have been engaging with lawyers to explore the prospect of seeking compensation from Manchester City for losses in possible bonus payments.
metadata.content: Man City charges: Premier League players and agents to explore compensation claims if club fail to overturn guilty verdict | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Man City charges: Premier League players and agents to explore compensation claims if club fail to overturn guilty verdict Premier League players and their agents are exploring the possibility of claims against Manchester City for loss of earnings if the club's guilty verdict is upheld after appeal; Man City have until Friday's deadline to lodge their appeal and deny any wrongdoing Amar Mehta News Editor Thursday 1 October 2026 16:17, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol answers more of your questions after Manchester City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission. Premier League players and their agents have been engaging with lawyers to explore the prospect of seeking compensation from Manchester City for losses in possible bonus payments. Several clubs have already instructed lawyers to assess the potential for litigation against City, should they fail to overturn the guilty verdict handed down by an independent commission this week. But it is not just clubs who could have grounds to sue. Sky Sports News understands that players have contacted lawyers over potential claims of their own. It is understood those claims relate to missed bonuses
